Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.
Additional Proposer(s) Use this section to identify additional individuals who can speak to the proposed program. Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the specialization to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.

College Select the college in which the program is housed.
Department Select the department in which the program is housed.

Is this interdisciplinary? The intent of this question is to identify whether the parent program of this specialization is jointly owned by multiple academic departments. If yes, the percentage of ownership assigned to each department must be provided in the curriculum worksheet.

Course Description
Tags: courses
Short Description: Student-facing summary of a course that clearly and concisely communicates its content, purpose, and focus.
Course Description
Course descriptions are written for students, not faculty, and must communicate clearly and concisely to them. Jargon, acronyms, and technical language should be avoided as much as possible. Anyone should be able to read the description and understand the nature and intent of the course.
An acceptable course description with a maximum of 30 words, begins with a verb, e.g. examines, introduces, explores, investigates. Articles, adjectives and adverbs are seldom necessary. Sentence fragments are acceptable.

Requisites
Tags: courses
Short Description: Courses or other requirements that must be completed before or at the time of enrollment in a course. Requisites may include prerequisites and corequisites.
Requisites
Requisites are courses, conditions, or other requirements that determine whether a student is eligible to enroll in a course. Requisites may be required before enrollment, at the time of enrollment, or may establish other conditions for registration.
Common types of requisites include:
Prerequisites: Courses or requirements that must be completed before enrolling in the course.
Corequisites: Courses or requirements that must be completed concurrently with the course.
Other enrollment requirements: Additional conditions that may apply to enrollment, such as minimum class standing, program or major restrictions, or other eligibility requirements.
When entering requisites in Kuali, ensure that the requirements accurately reflect the conditions under which students should be permitted to enroll.

Program Description
The University Catalog description of the requirements for completing an academic program, including the courses and credits required for the major, General Education, and free electives, as well as any additional program-specific requirements.

Descriptive overview: A brief paragraph explaining the purpose of the program and the significance of the degree or major.
Specializations: The specializations (sub-plans) should be listed by name, but the requirements should not be listed in the program description.
Major Requirements: Listed, required courses
Professional Electives: Students choose from a list of courses selected specifically to align with the content of the program
Free Electives: Students are free to choose. Must provide a credit amount, minimum 6 credits for undergraduate degrees are required
Cumulative GPA and/or major GPA requirements

Undergraduate programs shall include at least 6 credits of free electives (UM 8.21.10)
General Education requirements shall apply to all undergraduate programs (UM 8.21.11)
A cumulative average of at least 2.00 is required to graduate from all undergraduate degrees. (UM 8.22.10)
Master’s degree programs with thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. 18 must be from content-based courses, 6 must be thesis courses. (GSM 7.44.1)
Master’s degree programs without thesis require a minimum of 30 credits. (GSM 7.45.1)
Doctoral students must complete a Program of Study with a minimum of 64 credit hours beyond the undergraduate degree (GSM 7.54) (See GSM sections 7.54 and 7.21)

18 or more credits of related studies offered by one or more departments or programs and sponsored by a faculty member. (UM 8.20.50)
At least 12 credits at the 200-level or above ( UM 8.20.51)
At least 8 credits must be earned at URI (UM 8.20.51)
Minimum GPA average of 2.0 must be earned in the minor’s required courses (UM 8.20.51)
A maximum of two courses can apply to both the major and minor field of study (UM 8.20.52)

Undergraduate certificates generally require 15-21 credits of coursework (UM 8.20.70)
Undergraduate certificates are available to degree seeking and certificate-only seeking undergraduate students (UM 8.20.70)
Undergraduate certificate courses may not be pass/fail (UM 8.20.71)
